rules.title: FEHA housing discrimination: source-of-income protection and credit-history alternatives for subsidized applicants
rules.requirement: Owners may not discriminate against applicants or tenants because of source of income. Source of income means lawful, verifiable income, including public assistance and housing subsidies such as Section 8 vouchers and HUD-VASH vouchers. Owners may not publish ads indicating a source-of-income preference or make a dwelling unavailable on that basis. Income standards must count the aggregate income of persons residing together on the same basis as married couples. Where there is a government rent subsidy, owners must: (1) apply any financial or income standard only to the tenant's portion of the rent; and (2) not use credit history without offering the applicant the option to provide lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay, such as benefit payments, pay records or bank statements. The owner must give reasonable time to provide that evidence and must reasonably consider it in lieu of credit history. Owners may still verify employment, request landlord references, verify identity, and ask about the level or source of income.
rules.key_value: Source-of-income discrimination banned (incl. Section 8/HUD-VASH vouchers); for subsidized applicants, income standards apply only to the tenant's rent share, and credit history may be used only if alternative proof of ability to pay is offered
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to owners of any housing accommodation. The income-standard and credit-history provisions apply where there is a government rent subsidy.
rules.exemptions: Inquiry into the level or source of income is not discrimination. Verification of employment, landlord references and identity is permitted. A landlord is not a representative of a tenant unless the source of income is a HUD-VASH voucher.
rules.quoted_span: For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.conflict_note: The document states only the date of the latest amendment (Stats. 2023, Ch. 776, SB 267, effective January 1, 2024), which added the credit-history alternative-evidence provision. The underlying source-of-income protection predates that amendment, but the document gives no earlier effective date.
